title: Rolling Latency Average
summary: Maintain a time-windowed average latency per endpoint as measurements stream in.

stages.title: Windowed average
stages.requirement:
Build `LatencyMonitor(window_seconds)`:

- `record(endpoint, timestamp, latency_ms)` stores a measurement. Timestamps are integer
  seconds and **non-decreasing across all calls** (a single clock).
- `average(endpoint, now)` returns the mean latency of that endpoint's measurements with
  `now - window_seconds < timestamp <= now`, rounded to 2 decimals, or `None` if there are none.
  `now` is never earlier than the last recorded timestamp.

```python
m = LatencyMonitor(60)
m.record("/login", 0, 100)
m.record("/login", 30, 200)
m.average("/login", 30)   # -> 150.0
m.average("/login", 60)   # -> 200.0  (the t=0 sample left the window)
m.average("/search", 60)  # -> None
```

Expect up to 200,000 calls in total. Both methods should be amortized O(1).

visibleTests.name: test_example
visibleTests.code:
def test_example():
    m = LatencyMonitor(60)
    m.record("/login", 0, 100)
    m.record("/login", 30, 200)
    assert m.average("/login", 30) == 150.0
    assert m.average("/login", 60) == 200.0
    assert m.average("/search", 60) is None

hiddenTests.code:
def test_window_boundary_is_exclusive_on_the_left():
    m = LatencyMonitor(10)
    m.record("a", 5, 10)
    assert m.average("a", 14) == 10.0
    assert m.average("a", 15) is None

hiddenTests.name: test_endpoints_are_independent
hiddenTests.code:
def test_endpoints_are_independent():
    m = LatencyMonitor(100)
    m.record("a", 1, 10)
    m.record("b", 2, 30)
    assert m.average("a", 2) == 10.0
    assert m.average("b", 2) == 30.0

hiddenTests.description: Re-summing the whole window on every call is quadratic.

hints: Per endpoint, measurements leave the window in the same order they arrived.
Keep a deque of `(timestamp, latency)` and a running sum per endpoint. Evict from the left while the oldest is out of the window.
Evict lazily inside `average` (and optionally `record`). Each sample is appended and popped once, which gives amortized O(1).

solution.explanation:
Samples for an endpoint expire in arrival order, so a deque plus a running sum gives O(1)
amortized operations: append on `record`, pop from the left while the oldest timestamp
is `<= now - window`, and divide the running sum by the deque length. Every sample is
added and removed at most once.
